study type: Secondary analysis of data from the Maternal Fetal-Medicine Units Network Cesarean Registry
exposure: Cesarean delivery for arrest of dilation at 4-5 cm cervical dilation
Cesarean delivery for arrest of dilation at ≥ 6 cm cervical dilation
outcome: Composite maternal morbidity (chorioamnionitis, endometritis, transfusion, wound complication, operative injury, intensive care unit admission, or death)
cohort: Nulliparous women with term, singleton, vertex gestations who underwent primary cesarean delivery for arrest of dilation
finding: There was no significant difference in composite maternal or neonatal morbidity between cesarean delivery for arrest of dilation at 4-5 cm versus ≥ 6 cm cervical dilation.
